report.source_text: Flourescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and DNA mutation sequencing of the histiocytomas revealed a translocated KIF5B-ALK fusion rearrangement.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ALK+ histiocytosis with pathological features of juvenile xanthogranulomatosis (JXG)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-month-old full-term male infant presented with worsening tachypnoea and a rapidly enlarging, smooth-topped, infiltrative, bronze-yellow nodule with overlying telangiectasias on the mid-sternum. Skin and pulmonary biopsies demonstrated highly proliferative histiocytosis with ALK immunohistochemical positivity, CD33+, factor XIIIa+, and weakly CD68+, while being negative for CD1a, Langerin, CD34, CD20, CD3, CD43, SOX10, S100, C-KIT, lysozyme, and myeloperoxidase. Molecular analysis revealed a KIF5B-ALK fusion rearrangement. Whole-body imaging (MRI and PET/CT) confirmed extensive pulmonary lesions with spinal cord compression, a metabolically active right meningeal/parietal brain tumor, and extensive mediastinal/abdominal lymphadenopathy. Cladribine (2-CDA) chemotherapy was initiated due to the aggressive nature of ALK+ disease and systemic/CNS involvement. Follow-up PET imaging after six cycles demonstrated near-complete resolution of all FDG-avid lesions. The patient was subsequently transitioned to maintenance therapy with low-dose daily 6-mercaptopurine and weekly methotrexate, and currently remains in remission on follow-up radiological imaging.
